#3714900 [user] # mnemo — Agent Guide

mnemo is an MCP server that provides searchable memory across coding-agent
session transcripts. It maintains a realtime FTS5 index in SQLite and
ingests:

- **Claude Code** — `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (`source=claude`)
- **Codex CLI** — `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and
  `archived_sessions/` (`source=codex`; see `docs/design/codex-ingest.md`)
    10|- **Grok CLI** — `~/.grok/sessions/**/updates.jsonl` plus sibling
  `summary.json` (`source=grok`; honour `GROK_HOME`; see
  `docs/design/grok-ingest.md`)
- **Cursor Agent** — `~/.cursor/projects/**/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl`
  plus Agent CLI `~/.cursor/chats/**/store.db` for tool_result / cwd /
  title / model fidelity (🎯T149.1) (`source=cursor`; honour
  `CURSOR_HOME`; see `docs/design/cursor-ingest.md`). Resume:
  `agent --resume <id>`.

Filter or inspect provenance via `session_meta.source` (`mnemo_query`).
    20|
**Transcript file replay** (🎯T150 / 🎯T150.10) is a forensics recovery
tool: reconstruct agent file activity into a quarantine directory, seeding
pre-images from git (worktree/commit/stash), Grok rewind snapshots, Claude
file-history, and stitched Read tool_results before applying patches.

```bash
mnemo replay-files --session <id> --dry-run
mnemo replay-files --session <id>
mnemo replay-files --session <id> --seed-from HEAD
    30|mnemo replay-files --session <id> --no-seed   # Write/patch timeline only
mnemo replay-files --since 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z --until 2026-08-26T00:00:00Z --source cursor
```

Design: `docs/design/transcript-file-replay.md`. Never writes into a live
git checkout unless `--allow-live-tree` is set.

## Full setup (all steps required)

Installation is not complete until all four steps succeed. Do not stop
    40|after `brew install` — the server must be running and registered as an
MCP server for mnemo to be usable.

### 1. Install the binary

```bash
brew install marcelocantos/tap/mnemo
```

Or build from source (requires Go and CGo for SQLite):
    50|
```bash
GOWORK=off go build -tags "sqlite_fts5" -o bin/mnemo .
```

### 2. Start the server as a background service

**macOS (Homebrew)**:

```bash
    60|brew services start mnemo
```

This starts mnemo on `localhost:19419` via IPv4 and IPv6 loopback listeners
and keeps it running across reboots. Logs go to `$(brew --prefix)/var/log/mnemo.log`.

The Homebrew formula's service block sets `PATH` to
`$(brew --prefix)/bin:~/.claude/local:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`
so that mnemo's compactor can find the `claude` binary. If you run
mnemo via a different mechanism (custom launchctl plist, manual
    70|invocation), make sure `PATH` includes the directory containing
`claude` — typically `/opt/homebrew/bin` (npm/bun install) or
`~/.claude/local` (Anthropic's official installer). Without a `claude`
binary on `PATH`, compaction fails and mnemo logs an ERROR:
`compact: claude subprocess spawn failed — executable not found in PATH`.

**Linux (systemd)** — create `~/.config/systemd/user/mnemo.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
    80|Description=mnemo MCP server
... 668 lines not shown ...
#3714901 [user] ... 119 lines not shown ...
   120|does, and the rewritten tokens are identical, so the index converges.

The cursor survives restarts; a second run resumes at the last committed
batch, and a run over a finished table visits nothing. Progress is in
`op=compress_status`. Space comes back only with `VACUUM`, which needs
free disk equal to the database and blocks writers while it runs; it is
left to the operator.

The daemon enqueues the backfill itself (🎯T162) whenever it finds a
backlog of compressible plain rows — not only on upgrade or boot. The
   130|worker is batched, resumable, and yields between commits. A persisted
`done` marker stops the walk; re-appearance of plain rows clears it and
restarts. `compress.backfill` on doctor reports the phase and outstanding
plain bytes, and distinguishes bytes repacked from bytes reclaimed.
`compression.auto_backfill: false` pauses the worker. `op=compress_gc`
remains for an explicit one-family run.

## Ops

```
   140|mnemo_ops op=compress_status
mnemo_ops op=compress_train family=messages|docs
mnemo_ops op=compress_gc    family=messages|docs [wait=true]
```

`compress_gc` runs in the background by default because a full pass
over 5M rows runs for minutes, past any MCP call budget.

  T161:
    name: A refused start names who holds the port, not just that someone does
    status: identified
    value: 0.0
  3270|    cost: 0.0
    acceptance:
    - When the listen address is already bound, the message identifies the holding process — at minimum its pid, and its identity when determinable. The reported example shape is `port 19419 held by pid N (mnemo 0.93.0, lease EPZ-...); refusing to start`.
    - When the holder is another mnemo daemon, the message says so and distinguishes it from an unrelated process, because the two call for opposite responses from the operator.
    - 'Identification is best-effort and bounded: it never blocks startup beyond a short timeout, never turns a clean bind failure into a hang or crash, and degrades to today''s message (address plus underlying error) when the holder cannot be identified — including when lsof is absent, the normal case on a stock Windows box.'
    - Covered by a test that binds a port, starts mnemo against it, and asserts the message names the holding pid — not merely that some error was printed.
    context: |-
      The second half of point 3 of the owner's 2026-09-02 report, left as declared residue when 🎯T160 landed in v0.93.0.

      🎯T160 fixed the silent failure: main used to discard runServe's error, so a bind conflict exited 1 with zero bytes of output and, in the owner's words, "convincingly impersonated a second unrelated bug". v0.93.0 prints `mnemo: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:19419: bind: address already in use`.
  3280|
      That reports the error but not the holder, and the difference is the whole diagnostic value: "something is on this port" leaves the operator to go looking, whereas "your existing 0.93.0 daemon under launchd is on this port" ends the investigation. The two cases call for opposite responses — an expected daemon means the manual launch was redundant, an unrelated process means something needs moving.

      The pieces exist in-tree, so this is assembly rather than new machinery:

      - diagnose.go:211 already runs `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN -F pn`, yielding the listener's pid and command name, and already tolerates lsof being absent.
      - internal/upgrade/lease.go:86 forms a holder id as host:pid with a heartbeat file, so a mnemo holder can be recognised rather than guessed at.
      - lsof reports the executable path, which for a Homebrew install carries the version (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/mnemo/0.93.0/bin/mnemo).

      GET /health carries no version field — confirmed while verifying the v0.93.0 deploy, where a probe for one came back empty — so asking the holder over HTTP would need that added first. One option among several, not a prerequisite.
  3290|
      The bounded/best-effort requirement is not incidental: this runs on the failure path of startup, where the operator is already stuck, and a lookup that hangs there would be worse than the terse message it replaces.
    tags:

    - startup
    - cli
    - silent-failure
    origin: manual
    discovered: 2026-09-03
  T162:
  3300|    name: 'Compression finishes itself: historical rows get packed without anyone knowing an ops tool exists'
    status: achieved
    value: 0.0
    cost: 0.0
    attestation: 'Daemon enqueues historical-row packing itself: StartCompressBackfill is a goLoop started after AwaitSchemaUpgrade, triggered by a cheap outstanding-bytes probe per family (not boot/upgrade). Existing CompressBackfill stays batched/resumable; the auto path yields 10ms between batches. A done marker is reopened when compressible plain rows reappear (TestAutoBackfillRestartsWhenPlainRowsReappear). compress.backfill doctor check reports phase + outstanding plain bytes and says 0 reclaimed / VACUUM is manual. compression.auto_backfill defaults on; explicit false disables. Tests: TestAutoBackfillPacksPlainRowsWithoutAnOpsCall, TestAutoBackfillDisabledStaysOff, TestStartupCapabilitiesCheckReports sees the check. go test -tags sqlite_fts5 ./internal/store/ ./internal/registry/ ./internal/tools/ exit 0. Residue: the live 7.6 GiB store is not packed until this binary is deployed; VACUUM remains a manual operator step.'
    acceptance:
    - Historical rows are repacked without human intervention. The daemon enqueues the backfill itself, and completion does not depend on anyone knowing `mnemo_ops op=compress_gc` exists.
    - The trigger is a detected backlog of uncompressed rows, not merely an upgrade or a boot. A store that acquires a backlog by any route — restored backup, interrupted earlier run, a family whose dictionary trained later — converges without a release boundary to prompt it.
    - 'The work runs in the background and yields: batched, resumable across restarts, throttled under load, and never blocking normal reads or writes. A multi-gigabyte backfill is a long-running job, not a startup stall.'
    - Once a family has no plain rows left, the work stops and stays stopped — a persisted completion marker, not a full re-scan on every boot. Re-appearance of plain rows restarts it.
  3310|    - 'The residue is visible before it is fixed: a health check reports plain bytes still outstanding per family, so an unfinished migration cannot sit behind an all-green doctor. Whether it is running, complete, throttled or disabled is reported, in the manner of the images.embedder check.'
    - VACUUM stays manual and is not implied to have happened. Repacking empties the legacy columns but does not return the space to the filesystem, so any reporting distinguishes bytes repacked from bytes reclaimed.
    context: |-
      Reported by the owner 2026-09-03 against v0.93.0, on a 7.6 GiB store (mnemo.db = 8,136,052,736 bytes).

      The 🎯T151/🎯T152 migration trains dictionaries, switches new writes to compressed, and stops. Historical rows stay plain and nothing will ever repack them. Verified in the tree on 2026-09-03: `store.CompressBackfill` has exactly one caller, `compressGC` in internal/tools/consolidated_tools.go, which is reachable only from `mnemo_ops op=compress_gc`. internal/store/config.go contains no compression keys at all, and no check in internal/registry/diagchecks.go mentions compression. So this is not a feature left switched off — the automatic path was never built.

      Measured residue two days after migration: 4.96 GiB of 7.6 GiB still plain. messages.text 1,456 compressed of 686,056 rows (1.20 GiB plain); entries.raw 3,013 of 1,089,230 (3.72 GiB plain); docs.content 0 of 3,360 (35.5 MiB) — a job the owner notes would take seconds. The compressed counts are only the rows written since the dictionaries went active, which also confirms the write path is working correctly and that compress_gc is pure historical catch-up rather than a switch that enables anything.

      What makes it quiet is precisely that the write path works: the feature looks delivered while the bulk of the win never arrives. The migration's own timestamps show the deliberate stop — pre-migration snapshot at 21:24:14Z, all three dictionaries trained at 21:26:29-30Z on 3,000-row samples, then nothing. Filtering the daemon log for compress/dictionary/zstd/backfill returns only segment backfill, a different subsystem that does run automatically. Nothing is stuck; nothing is scheduled.
  3320|
      The owner's sharpest point is about the diagnostic surface: `mnemo_ops op=doctor` reports 18 ok / 0 warn / 0 fail, and those 18 include images.embedder, which cheerfully reports that an opt-in feature is disabled. A permanently unfinished migration holding ~5 GiB is invisible on the surface built to make exactly this visible.

      Recoverable space is estimated at 2.5-3 GiB from per-row packed-vs-plain ratios of roughly 0.63 (messages) and 0.37 (entries). The owner marks this indicative only: it extrapolates from recently-written rows to the whole historical population, and recent rows need not be representative. Second-order cost: every backup snapshot carries the uncompressed bulk, and the backup design's peak-disk note is sized against an unnecessarily large database.

      The owner's prescription, followed in the acceptance above: enqueue the backfill after training as a low-priority background task, batched and resumable (which compress_gc already is), yielding under load; trigger whenever a backlog is found rather than only on upgrade or startup; allow normal operation throughout; set a flag once complete to suppress further activity. VACUUM stays manual — it needs free disk equal to the database plus temp, and a quiet moment.
    tags:
    - compression
    - disk
    - migration
  3330|    - silent-failure
    - background-work
    origin: manual
    discovered: 2026-09-03
    achieved: 2026-09-03
  T163:
    name: Compactor deferrals do not accrue toward quarantine, so a non-payload reply cannot exile a session
    status: achieved
    value: 0.0
    cost: 0.0
  3340|    attestation: 'Watcher no longer records outcomeDeferred via RecordCompactionFailure (watcher.go); TestWatcherDefersNonPayload asserts zero RecordCompactionFailure calls and a deferred count. SelectCompactionCandidates and QuarantinedCount ignore last_error=deferred. ClearDeferredQuarantine deletes leftover deferred rows and runs at watcher start. TestSelectCompactionCandidatesIgnoresDeferredQuarantine covers a pre-existing deferred row staying eligible. go test -tags sqlite_fts5 ./internal/compact/ ./internal/store/ ./internal/registry/ ./internal/tools/ exit 0. Residue: live daemon still v0.93.0 until this ships — the three fail_count=88 rows clear on the next start.'
    acceptance:
    - A deferred tick (summariser returned a well-formed response that is not a JSON payload) does not call RecordCompactionFailure and does not increment fail_count. The outcome remains visible as deferred in the watcher's counts so the ratio still distinguishes it from compacted and from failed.
    - Existing compactor_quarantine rows whose last_error is deferred are cleared so they no longer exclude a session. After this, a session that was sitting at fail_count 88 with last_error = deferred is eligible again and can be summarised.
    - The candidate query's quarantine predicate does not treat last_error = deferred as a failure. Only hard failures and timeouts accrue toward the threshold and keep a session excluded.
    - A session that keeps producing non-payloads is retried on later scans (subject to the existing per-scan cap and breaker), not parked indefinitely with addenda above budget. Persistently-broken sessions that actually fail still quarantine.
    - Covered by a test that ticks a non-payload session and asserts zero RecordCompactionFailure calls, and by a test that a pre-existing deferred quarantine row does not exclude the session.
    context: |-
      The leftover from the owner's 2026-09-02 email (the stdin/self-install report that became 🎯T160/🎯T161). Quoted: "Four sessions quarantined, three of them at fail_count 88 with last_error = deferred. backlog sits at 3 and every tick reports nothing_to_compact, so those sessions are never summarised and their addenda stay above budget indefinitely. A deferral isn't a failure and shouldn't accrue toward the quarantine threshold. Table is compactor_quarantine; only ad5a6244 shows a real failed."

  3350|      🎯T77 classified ErrNoPayload as not a hard failure in the failed:compacted ratio, but still recorded it via RecordCompactionFailure so a session that kept producing conversational replies would eventually quarantine. That second half is the bug: the durable table does not distinguish deferred from failed, so three sessions hit fail_count 88 on deferred alone and dropped out of SelectCompactionCandidates. Once excluded they can never clear the row (clear happens on a successful tick, which they never get), so addenda sit above budget forever.

      Verified in the tree on 2026-09-03: watcher.go:471 folds outcomeDeferred into the same RecordCompactionFailure arm as outcomeFailed and outcomeTimeout, and the comment on outcomeDeferred still says it accrues toward quarantine. TestWatcherDefersNonPayload asserts that recording. The owner's report is the reversal of that T77 clause.
    tags:
    - compactor
    - quarantine
    - silent-failure
    origin: manual
    discovered: 2026-09-03
    achieved: 2026-09-03
  3360|  T17:
    name: Every mnemo stream self-heals on startup — no agent should need to know whether a given mnemo_* tool has seen the whole corpus
    status: achieved

#3714903 [user] ... 299 lines not shown ...
   300|
Off by default. When enabled, mnemo watches for new releases and
applies them during a quiet window, preserving open connections. Only
**Homebrew non-Windows** installs actually auto-apply; every other
install (Windows, source builds) stays notify-only regardless of this
setting, surfacing the new release through `upgrade.available` and
leaving the upgrade to you.

## Registering as an MCP server

   310|**Claude Code** (global install to `~/.claude.json`):

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http mnemo http://localhost:19419/mcp
```

**Grok Build** (writes `~/.grok/config.toml`):

```bash
grok mcp add --transport http mnemo http://localhost:19419/mcp
   320|```

**Generic MCP client** JSON config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mnemo": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:19419/mcp"
   330|    }
  }
}
```

Restart your agent session after registration — tools registered
mid-session are not picked up.

Before restarting, confirm the server is listening:

   340|```bash
lsof -iTCP:19419 -sTCP:LISTEN
```

Do **not** use `curl` to probe `/mcp` — MCP endpoints only respond to
POST requests with a JSON-RPC body. After restart, call `mnemo_stats`.

#3714917 [user] ... 499 lines not shown ...
   500|`op=doctor` is the first thing to reach for when something looks wrong —
a per-check health report (ok/warn/fail plus remediation) covering the
summariser workdir, `claude` on PATH, configured roots, the compaction
circuit-breaker, backfill progress and database responsiveness. The same
data backs `GET /health` and the dashboard.

`op=backup_status` reports the retained snapshots AND the total bytes in
the backup directory. When those disagree, the difference is scratch
from an interrupted run; the daemon sweeps its own (`.backup-*.db` and
its `-journal`/`-wal`/`-shm` siblings, plus `mnemo-*.tmp`) once over six
   510|hours old, and the `backup.disk` check in
`op=doctor` warns about the rest. Every snapshot path — daily worker,
`op=backup_now`, pre-migration — prunes to the configured retention,
which defaults to one.

`op=compactor` is the compaction diagnostic: tick counts include
`deferred` vs `failed`, and the quarantined count excludes deferrals
(🎯T163). A deferred tick (summariser returned a well-formed
non-payload) is not a failure and does not increment `fail_count`.
Leftover `last_error=deferred` rows are cleared on watcher start. Only
   520|hard failures and timeouts accrue toward quarantine.

`op=compress_status` reports dictionary and cursor state.
`op=compress_gc` is an explicit one-family override of the automatic
backfill (🎯T162); leave it alone unless you have paused
`compression.auto_backfill`.

`op=restore` is destructive and requires an explicit `session_id`.

An unknown op answers with the valid list, and a parameter belonging to
   530|a different op is **rejected rather than ignored**, so a wrong guess
fails loudly instead of silently doing something else.

### mnemo_thread

Thread navigation: `op=list|show|new|archive|go`. Same data as the
daemon's `/api/thread/*` endpoints, which the menubar app uses.

  210:**v0.93.0 note (🎯T160)**: mnemo runs the HTTP daemon, and only the

./docs/audit-log.md
  487:## 2026-09-02 — /release v0.93.0
  489:- **Outcome**: Released v0.93.0. 🎯T160: the stdio modality is purged outright rather than deprecated. mnemo inferred its invocation mode from whether stdin was a character device, so supervisord's stdin pipe sent it down a legacy-stdio fallback that rewrote `~/.claude.json`, ran `brew services start mnemo` (installing a `KeepAlive=true` launchd job that outlived the config creating it), and exited 1 — mnemo never stayed up under a process supervisor. Removed `stdinPiped`, `autoMigrateStdioAndExit`, the manual-migration hint, and `portInUse`/`localhostDialTargets`; bare `mnemo` is unconditionally the HTTP daemon and no code path installs or starts mnemo as a service (`brew services restart` in the opt-in auto-upgrade path is retained deliberately). Two ratchets plus a behavioural test that hands the process a pipe on stdin; validated as an oracle by running the released v0.92.0 binary under the same repro, where it fails all three assertions. Also fixed: `main` discarded `runServe`'s er [... omitted end of long line]

    Release prep for v0.93.0, and document the argv surface honestly
    
    Version bump, the v0.93.0 audit-log entry, and three documentation
    fixes the release audit surfaced.
    
    agents-guide.md ships inside the binary as --help-agent, so it is what
    an agent reads when mnemo misbehaves — and it had a diagnostic path for
    "the server isn't running" but none for "it exited immediately". That is
    the failure 🎯T160 was about: a bind conflict used to produce no output
    at all and impersonated an unrelated bug. Both it and the README now
    show the message and say plainly that a port already in use means the
    daemon is up, not broken.
    
    STABILITY.md's CLI tables were the authoritative "here is mnemo's whole
    argv surface" listing and were missing two flags (--help-config, --home)
    and five subcommands (thread, resume, budget, edge, replay-files) —
    verified against main.go's dispatch rather than taken on trust. Both
    gaps predate this release, but the table is exactly where a reader would
    look to find out whether a stdio mode exists, so it now says outright
    that it does not.

#3715421 [user] # Stability

## Stability commitment

Once mnemo reaches 1.0, backwards compatibility becomes a binding
contract. Breaking changes to the CLI interface, MCP tool signatures,
configuration, or database schema will not be made without forking to a
new product. The pre-1.0 period exists to get these surfaces right.

    10|## Interaction surface catalogue

Snapshot as of v0.33.0, amended for the 🎯T143 tool-surface reduction
(see the v0.84.0 and v0.85.0 notes below).

**v0.88.0 note**: Default local MCP/API bind is dual-stack loopback
(`tcp4 127.0.0.1:19419` and `tcp6 [::1]:19419`) instead of all
interfaces. The implicit default uses the `localhost:19419` sentinel
and expands before listen; a missing address family on one side is
non-fatal. Explicit `--addr :19419` remains the deliberate LAN-exposure
    20|bind. Self-check and diagnose URLs target an address that actually
bound. Matches the documented localhost-only trust model for the
auth-less local surface. mTLS federation (`--federated-addr`) is
unchanged.

**v0.84.0 / v0.85.0 note — MCP tool surface reduced from 70 tools to 18
(🎯T143, 🎯T144).** This is the largest breaking change to the tool
surface before 1.0, and it is deliberately made now: this document's own
commitment is that backwards compatibility binds at 1.0 and "the pre-1.0
period exists to get these surfaces right". An audit on 2026-08-07 found
    30|that of 70 registered tools, only 40 had ever been called by an agent and
15 in the previous 30 days, with `mnemo_search` alone accounting for 55%
of all calls.

The reduction landed in two waves. v0.84.0 took 70 → 38 by deleting
dead tools and consolidating families behind an `op` parameter. v0.85.0
took 38 → 18 by deleting a further eighteen tools whose whole function
was to wrap a query shape that `mnemo_query` already expresses, and by
folding two search pathways into `mnemo_search` itself (🎯T144).

    40|*Removed in v0.85.0 as query wrappers with no replacement*:
... 810 lines not shown ...
#3715422 [user] ... 479 lines not shown ...
   480|
- **Outcome**: Released v0.91.0. Configuration is file-only with `mnemo --help-config` (🎯T156); `mnemo_config` and `mnemo_note` removed, tool surface down ~32% by weight to 16 tools. Backups compress with vendored multithreaded libzstd (🎯T159): 8.5s at 2132 MB/s on an 18.2 GB index against gzip -1's ~83 MB/s, and every snapshot is now verified by decompression before the previous one is retired (retention is one snapshot, 🎯T158). `backup.Decompress` reads both `.db.zst` and `.db.gz`, so pre-release snapshots stay restorable without the zstd CLI. Documentation pass: repaired five empty README tool tables and a section documenting a removed tool, corrected the tool count (27 → 16) and the federated-tool count (16 → 4), rewrote the agent guide's schema section to point at the generated catalogue and to read through `messages_v`/`docs_v`/`entries_v` (its examples had been silently returning empty text since per-row compression landed), and closed four `NOTICE` attribution gaps including the two AWS modules' mandatory NOTICE content. Added a `workflow_dispatch` dry run to `release.yml` so the three build targets CI never covers are proven before the tag.

## 2026-08-31 — /release v0.92.0

- **Outcome**: Released v0.92.0. 🎯T158 in full: retention became part of taking a backup (`backup.CreateAndRetain`), replacing a single-call-site `GCOldest` that left the pre-migration path and `op=backup_now` pruning nothing — enforced by a ratchet test over new callers of the raw API, with the one exemption (the migration path) held to its promise by a test. Added `SweepOrphans` for stranded `.backup-*.db` VACUUM temps and `mnemo-*.tmp`, running at startup even when backups are disabled, guarded by an in-process live-temp registry plus a 6h age threshold. Fixed `Backup` leaking `destPath.tmp` on a non-compressor failure (found by an injected-failure test) and a same-second `Filename` collision that silently overwrote a snapshot (found by calling `op=backup_now` twice). `op=backup_status` now reports bytes on disk vs retained, and a new `backup.disk` health check warns on unaccounted bytes or an over-retention snapshot count. Verified live against an isolated daemon: a planted 2 GiB day-old orphan was swept at startup, a 2-minute-old one spared, and `op=backup_now` reported pruning.

## 2026-09-02 — /release v0.93.0

- **Outcome**: Released v0.93.0. 🎯T160: the stdio modality is purged outright rather than deprecated. mnemo inferred its invocation mode from whether stdin was a character device, so supervisord's stdin pipe sent it down a legacy-stdio fallback that rewrote `~/.claude.json`, ran `brew services start mnemo` (installing a `KeepAlive=true` launchd job that outlived the config creating it), and exited 1 — mnemo never stayed up under a process supervisor. Removed `stdinPiped`, `autoMigrateStdioAndExit`, the manual-migration hint, and `portInUse`/`localhostDialTargets`; bare `mnemo` is unconditionally the HTTP daemon and no code path installs or starts mnemo as a service (`brew services restart` in the opt-in auto-upgrade path is retained deliberately). Two ratchets plus a behavioural test that hands the process a pipe on stdin; validated as an oracle by running the released v0.92.0 binary under the same repro, where it fails all three assertions. Also fixed: `main` discarded `runServe`'s error, so a bind conflict exited 1 with zero bytes of output — measured 0 bytes before, an explicit `bind: address already in use` after. `mnemo diagnose` keeps recognising mcpbridge wrappers (that entry's stdio transport is the bridge's, not mnemo's).
   490|
